Can you explain what LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is in simple terms?

Think of a large language model like an enormous encyclopedia of knowledge containing billions of pre-printed pages. 

Instead of rewriting all those billions of pages during fine-tuning (which requires massive GPU memory), **LoRA** leaves the encyclopedia frozen. Instead, it clips a lightweight notepad of two small mathematical matrices ($A$ and $B$) onto each layer. When $A$ and $B$ are multiplied together, they produce the low-rank updates needed for your specific task.

This reduces the trainable parameters by over 99% while keeping almost all the quality!
